What is more, they won this event, beating the North team composed of Pettit, Metcalfe, Chapman and Day. Also in the programme were a 2 Miles Walk—and here again we have to thank the R.W.A. secretary for his very kind co-operation—and one field event: the Weight Put.
440 Yards.—2, Jarlett (Bel.); 3, Watts (Bel.). 63.6. 880 Yards.—1, Pettit (Bel.); 2, Sheail (Bel.)—2.34. 1 Mile.—1, Police; 2, Cohen (Bel.); 4, Morrell.—4.40.

Bell, Cyril Forey maintained our place and thus it was that Charlie's unfortunate, but memorable run began. Day's fastest. - Edelen (Chelms) 14:35 Batty (Thurrock) 14:36 Pettit (Ayles) 14:42 Herring (B'Hth) 14:49.
Few people would have given the Belgrave team of Kerr, Crookes and Paget much hope against that renowned trio from Aylesford P.M. - Mayatt, Pettit and Minshall.

Trevor Hart knocked 17 secs off Pettit's lap record for the next stage to move us up to 2nd and a back-in-form Gerry North followed suit by lopping 24 secs off Ellis's record to put us way out in front.
Beagler Dan Pettit made up ground on “Sharpy” and the two were locked together for much of the stage, working off each other as they slowly pulled back Aldershot’s colours, carried by Eliot Robinson.
